::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 3d 1860  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection, C0171: Box 29
:::

Dear [Miss Erskine](people/person_489.qmd),

Many thanks for so kindly enquiring to satisfy the Salisbury correspondent. I will wait till this day week to answer him; in case you should have more particulars for me, I wonder whether he wants to make any use of the story, which should I am sure be widely known, I have no longer the address of Miss [Blanch Shelley](people/person_1822.qmd) who sent it to me, and with whom it was a tradition from an aunt. I should think she knew no more, as she gave no names when I wrote to her for corroboration before inserting it, and she only knew half the story. I am glad to hear such good accounts of [Mrs](people/person_462.qmd) and [Miss Dyson](people/person_464.qmd), I hoped to have seen them again this summer, but it seems as if it would not be till they go to Testwood.[^1] [Mary Coleridge](people/person_351.qmd) seemed fairly well, and very animated and bright when I spent an evening with her when she was in London

Yours very truly

C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The home of Anne Sturges Bourne.
